## Overview
This vignette demonstrates how to optimise the BANKSY* clustering parameters used by SpatialCopyInference. We compare different combinations of BANKSY smoothing `lambda` and clustering `resolution` to identify settings that best capture spatially coherent SCNA-defined populations.

To reproduce this example, first download the Xenium ovarian cancer dataset from:
<https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/xenium-prime-ffpe-human-ovarian-cancer>

```{r Import data example paths, eval = FALSE}
# Path to Xenium output directory
data_dir <- "path/to/Xenium_outputs/outs"

# Path to refined cell type annotations
annotation_file <- "path/to/cell_type_annotations.csv"
```

```{r}
# Load SpatialCopyInference
library(SpatialCopyInference)

# Import data
xenium.obj <- import_xenium(data_dir, annotation_file)

# Quality control
xenium.obj <- filter_cells(xenium.obj)
xenium.obj <- filter_genes(xenium.obj, min_cells = 50, min_counts = 50)

# Normalisation
xenium.obj <- normalise_data(xenium.obj)

# Compute chromosome arm means 
arm_means <- compute_arm_means(xenium.obj, min_genes_per_arm = 5)

# SCNA inference
arm_ratios <- compute_arm_ratios(arm_means, 
                                 xenium.obj,
                                 group_var = "group",
                                 reference = c("Fallopian Tube Epithelium", "Secretory Epithelial Cells"))
```
## Spatial clustering optimisation
Here we compare multiple combinations of `lambda` and `resolution`.

### Lambda = 0.8
```{r, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
BANKSY.obj <- compute_spatial_clusters(
  arm_ratios = arm_ratios,
  xenium.obj = xenium.obj,
  lambda = 0.8,
  resolution = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.5)
)

heatmaps <- plot_cluster_heatmaps(
  BANKSY.obj,
  resolutions = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.5)
)
```

### Lambda = 0.2
```{r, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
BANKSY.obj_02 <- compute_spatial_clusters(
  arm_ratios = arm_ratios,
  xenium.obj = xenium.obj,
  lambda = 0.2,
  resolution = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.5)
)

heatmaps_02 <- plot_cluster_heatmaps(
  BANKSY.obj_02,
  resolutions = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.5)
)
```


## Summary
Optimisation of the mixing parameter (λ) and clustering resolution (res) enabled stable cluster identification, with λ = 0.8 and res = 0.1 providing the clearest separation of biologically distinct populations.
